title: Jamaica's 1988 bobsled team
hook: A country with no snow sent a bobsled team to the 1988 Winter Olympics.
peek: Two Americans watching a Jamaican pushcart derby saw racers who could sprint and push a cart. They decided Jamaica should try the bobsled, and in 1988 a team of Jamaican soldiers arrived at the Calgary Winter Olympics.
lede: Bobsled races are often won in the first few seconds, when the crew sprints and shoves the sled before jumping in. In the mid 1980s, two Americans living in Jamaica, George Fitch and William Maloney, watched a local pushcart derby and saw exactly that skill. Jamaica has no snow, but it has fast runners. By 1988 it had an Olympic bobsled team.

bullets.text: Fitch and Maloney first hoped to sign up top sprinters, but none were keen. They turned to the Jamaica Defence Force instead, and soldiers including Dudley Stokes and Devon Harris became the core of the team, learning on borrowed sleds.

At the 1988 Calgary Games the four-man sled tipped over on its final run. The crew climbed out and walked their sled over the finish line to warm applause, which became one of the defining images of the Games.

The bobsled team's story inspired the 1993 Disney film Cool Runnings. It kept the spirit but invented much of the detail, including the characters and the coach, so the real team's story is quieter than the film's.
The team kept going. At the 1994 Lillehammer Games, Jamaica's four-man sled finished 14th, ahead of crews from several countries with long winters and long bobsled traditions.
